what_slowed_or_broke: PLAN_2026-11.md and hardening/STATUS.md were absent from master and from the session branch; found only by git log --all on origin/ccr-888d8b52-lzcqoe (2 docs commits ahead of master)
root_cause: plan commits were pushed to a session branch and never merged into master before the step sessions were started
fix_idea: merge the plan+STATUS commits to master (or point every step session at the plan branch) before launching step sessions

what_slowed_or_broke: fresh cloud container has no tensorflow/pandas pins: every test that loads trainer/model (and the pre-change fingerprint) failed with ModuleNotFoundError until pip install -r requirements-ci.txt
root_cause: the environment setup script does not install requirements-ci.txt; the SessionStart hook only sets core.hooksPath
fix_idea: install requirements-ci.txt in the environment setup script (or the SessionStart hook) so step sessions can run tests immediately

what_slowed_or_broke: core.registry.Registry was not a drop-in for dict reads (get() raises on unknown, items() returned Entry objects, no [] access) so 'keep the dict read API' needed an additive adapter and caller edits (.get(x) -> .get(x, None))
root_cause: the primitive was written in PR 0 before any consumer existed; no consumer-driven API check
fix_idea: when adding a primitive, migrate one real consumer in the same PR or write the consumer-shaped test first

what_slowed_or_broke: full local pytest run (with Pandas4Warning as error) takes >50 min; the background run died at ~87% when the session restarted, and a pgrep-based 'still running' check matched its own command line, so a dead run was reported as running; the review then found 14+ extra unnormalised timeframe sites that only a repo-wide AST scan (not the test run) could list
root_cause: no sharded or time-boxed test entry point and no repo-wide guard for deprecated-API patterns, so completeness of a deprecation fix was only discoverable by grep after the PR
fix_idea: add a tools/ test runner that shards tests/ and writes a resumable report; keep AST guards (tests/test_timeframe_normalize.py) as the completeness check for each deprecation fix

what_slowed_or_broke: plan said the timing callback separates input-pipeline wait from compute; on Keras 3 the batch is fetched inside the train_function call so begin->end covers both (measured with a deliberately slow tf.data map: wait ~0 ms, compute = fetch + step); had to add an input-only probe instead
root_cause: plan step written without checking what Keras 3 callbacks can observe
fix_idea: state in plan steps which measurement is assumed possible, or spike it before writing the spec

what_slowed_or_broke: PR #61 was already merged when the session started while the session branch still held the old pre-merge tip; the first push attempt used --force-with-lease and was denied before checking that a plain fast-forward was enough
root_cause: the restart-from-master recipe in the session prompt suggests force-with-lease although origin's branch tip is an ancestor of master after a merge commit
fix_idea: check `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<branch> HEAD` first; push without force when true

what_slowed_or_broke: tools/ cannot import tests/ or docs/ (check_deps) so the namespace-loading helpers of docs/research/audit/_nbload.py and tests/run_fixture.py had to be re-implemented in tools/profile_run.py (build_namespace)
root_cause: the shared-namespace loading recipe (which modules to exclude per package) lives only in test helpers and in tools/evaluate_trained_model.py's notebook runner
fix_idea: lift a `build_namespace()` into a code package (workflow or tools) and let tests and tools call it (S24 candidate)
